276740987.description:
Geoscience Industries
Introductory Earth Science Collection
2000, 75 Specimen Set
A comprehensive introductory geology kit designed for educational use, produced by Geoscience Industries in 2000. This collection is organized to teach the Mohs scale of mineral hardness and classifications for igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks. It serves as a classic classroom resource or a foundational set for a budding mineralogist, featuring a variety of textures and compositions typical of earth science studies.
75-slot display tray with numbered identification system matching the included guide
Includes original classification sheet covering rock-forming minerals and ore types
Bonus items: Handheld magnifying glass, large selenite wand, polished banded agate disc, and several loose tumbled stones
Dimensions: 20 inches (L) x 11.5 inches (W) x 2 inches (H)
Condition:
This is a partial set; approximately 40 of the 75 original numbered specimens are present, with several slots empty or containing only small fragments. The outer cardboard sleeve shows heavy wear, including a significant tear and crushing at one corner and visible staining. The foam protector and plastic tray remain intact and functional. The identification sheet shows light handling wear. Includes additional loose stones not original to the 75-piece set.
Thank you for all of your support!

276548591.description:
Orthoceras Fossil Specimen Polished Nautiloid Cephalopod Shell Display
This fossil specimen features two Orthoceras fossils embedded in a dark gray to black matrix rock. Orthoceras is an extinct genus of nautiloid cephalopod characterized by long, tapered, conical shells with visible internal chamber lines. The matrix rock is rough and unpolished on the back and sides, while the fossilized shells on the front are polished to a glossy finish, highlighting their natural details and structure. The piece is in excellent natural condition with no visible repairs, suitable for fossil collectors or natural history displays.

276637525.description:
Natural Agate Geode Specimen
Polished Chalcedony with Druzy Crystal Center
Natural Earth Tone Aesthetic
This natural agate geode features exquisite concentric banding in shades of steel blue, soft grey, and translucent white. Formed within volcanic rock cavities, this specimen showcases the transition from cryptocrystalline chalcedony to macrocrystalline quartz, culminating in a delicate druzy-lined central aperture. The contrast between the polished face and the raw, unrefined exterior highlights the unique geological processes that create these treasures.
Polished face highlights natural growth rings and rhythmic agate banding
Rough, unpolished matrix exterior in deep purple and grey tones
Small central vug lined with sparkling clear quartz druzy crystals
Flat-cut base allows for upright display on desks or shelves
Measures approximately 3 inches by 2.5 inches
Condition:
Good condition with a high-polish finish on the display face. The natural rock exterior remains in its original rough state with no structural cracks or repairs. There are no notable stains or surface scratches on the polished area.
